chapter_theme: The quarrel of the six sects (அறுசமயப் பிணக்கம்): the six systems seek the Lord outside and miss the God who stands within the body; he is not the substance of any sect, and those who argue that this one or that one is good stay deluded and are born and die. The way is Siva's path, the guru's word and the light within, where no quarrel remains.
structure_note: Three movements: the sects miss the God within (1530 to 1533); Siva's path alone saves and the sects are waste (1534 to 1541); the Lord to be sought without distinction, and the inner light that ends the quarrel (1542 to 1549). The heading's word பிணக்கு appears only in 1547.

1530.reading: The six sects that stand in the assembly do not see the God who stands within the body; caught in the bond of house and children, they fall writhing into the pit of maya.
1530.nuance: ஆயத்துள் (in the assembly) is set against காயத்துள் (in the body), a near rhyme that carries the argument: the sects look in the crowd and miss the body. Which six sects are meant the verse doesn't say; tradition gives several lists.

1531.reading: They do not know the purpose of the One who hid within the heart and stands everywhere, the generous chief, the great ascetic dwelling in the flower, the thief-chief who enters and leaves the hollow hut of the body.
1531.nuance: பொள்ளற் குரம்பை (the hut full of holes) is the body with its nine openings. கள்ளத் தலைவன் (the thief-chief) is the Lord who comes and goes unseen. மலருறை மாதவன் may be the great ascetic in the heart's lotus or a name of Vishnu given to the one Lord; the verse doesn't settle it.

1532.reading: For those who say he is within and without, our Lord is within and without; for those who say he is neither within nor without, he is neither within nor without.
1532.nuance: A mirror verse. It can be read as the Lord appearing to each as each conceives him, or as an irony at the sects: what they say decides what they find. It doesn't say which view is right.

1533.reading: Those who saw the six sects did not see him; he is not the thing the six sects hold; be clear, and having become clear, settle, and once settled you may enter the house without wavering.
1533.nuance: தேறுமின், தேறித் தெளிமின், தெளிந்தபின் chains clarity to clarity. மனை (house, home) is read as release, the home one does not leave; it may also be plain household life lived without wavering.

1534.reading: There is nothing but Siva, I declare; for those who reach him here there is nothing but the austerity that is Siva; the six sects are nothing but waste: cling to the feet of Nandi, strong in austerity, and be saved.
1534.nuance: சிவம், தவம், அவம் rhyme through three lines. அறையே may be 'I proclaim' or a call. நந்தி may be Siva himself or Tirumular's teacher; the tradition uses the name for both. The line breaks are uncertain (யறையே சிவமாந் / தவம்).

1535.reading: The six sects that sought the Lord, longing greatly to become gods, perish where they stand because they did not strive within, and so do not know the way to leave the earth.
1535.nuance: முண்ணின் றழியு முயன்றிலர் is unclear: perhaps உண்ணின்று (within) with a misprint, as read here. விண்ணவராக (to become gods) faults the sects for seeking heaven rather than release from birth.

1536.reading: Siva's path is the only path; all others are paths of becoming, and in them is a birth in bonds; if the path of austerity shows itself straight, the three of the wasted path are of that same kind.
1536.nuance: சிவகதி, பவகதி, தவகதி, அவகதி play on கதி (path, end). Lines 3 and 4 are obscure: அவகதி மூவரும் may be the three gods (Brahma, Vishnu, Rudra) as ends in becoming, or three classes of the lost.

1537.reading: Counted out, there are a hundred sects, and they fall within the six; the sects that are spoken of do not stay in the path they took; the end, the supreme path, is no path of theirs.
1537.nuance: ஆறு சமயமவ் ஆறுட் படுவன may also read 'the six sects fall within those six' (the six inner sects of Saivism). The last line, ஈறு பரநெறி யில்லா நெறியன்றே, can be parsed as 'the supreme path is not a path without an end' or as read here; it is unclear.

1538.reading: The wretched are like braying donkeys; pure Siva stands everywhere untouched, but not understanding the one who removes faults, takes up good qualities and cherishes, they go mad and are born and die every day.
1538.nuance: The third line echoes Tiruvasagam (Ammanai), where குற்றங்கள் நீக்கிக் குணங்கொண்டு கோதாட்டி describes the Lord, which fixes its sense: the Lord is the one who removes faults and cherishes, and the deluded don't know him. தோய்வற்று (untouched) says Siva pervades without being stained.

1539.reading: Whether bewildered or clear of mind, if people unite and drive the two deeds into the cave's mouth and, moving on, attain, then when the end is shown there is a supreme path for those whose fear is gone.
1539.nuance: முழைமுகப் பாச்சி (driving into the mouth of the cave) is obscure; it may be yogic, the breath driven into an inner opening. The point that both the confused and the clear can reach the path is the plainest part.

1540.reading: Far and near, without affliction, named Nandi, pure to those who can look without wavering: people bewildered by the deceiver do not know the purpose the body serves.
1540.nuance: மாயன் may be Vishnu, often named the deluder, or maya personified. காயம் விளைக்குங் கருத்து (the intent the body produces) is read as the purpose for which the body is given; it may also mean the thoughts the body breeds.

1541.reading: There is one seed for both ways: the blame of living on earth and clinging to it; those on the ruinous path do not stand before the word of the one who knows the whirl to seek the way.
1541.nuance: வழி இரண்டு (both ways) is unexplained. சுழியறிவாளன் (the one who knows the whirl) is taken as the guru who knows the inner point (சுழி) of yoga. The verse is compressed and its grammar uncertain.

1542.reading: All the great ascetics say Mahadeva is the Lord; Nandi is to be known as nada; if, without making distinctions, you worship with folded hands calling him Lord, the First himself stands as that path.
1542.nuance: பேதஞ்செய்யாதே (without making distinctions) answers the chapter's quarrel: the remedy is not one sect's victory but worship that does not divide. நாதமதாக அறியப்படு (known as nada) gives the Lord a mantra-form.

1543.reading: Hara's path, the Father, the First Lord, who became the strong path and entered the heart: if the minds of devotees who seek the supreme path do not become the Supreme's path, they are many kinds of distance away.
1543.nuance: நெறி (path) ends every line: Hara's path, the strong path, the supreme path, the Supreme's path. The claim is that devotion itself must become the path, not merely seek it.

1544.reading: He knows each one's nature, he is good, he is the sun; he shines in the attainment of those of great knowledge; think of him without fault, the pure gem-coloured one: rare is the path of virtue he set.
1544.nuance: பரிசறிவான் may be 'he who knows the measure (of each)' or 'he who knows the gift'. அரிது (rare, hard) in the last line may say his path is hard to walk or precious.

1545.reading: Give up the delusion of deluded men who say this sect or that one is good; seek the God beyond the forest, whose form is beyond all lack.
1545.nuance: கானம் may be the forest (the wild of worldly life) or, as some take it, song; ஊனம் (lack, flaw) also means flesh, so ஊனங் கடந்த உரு may be a form beyond the flesh. The verse rejects the ranking of sects, not worship.

1546.reading: Seeking that path, the immortals and sages saw the red path and were made Siva; those without the First's grace, who seek the earlier paths, do not go on the red path, and so are bewildered.
1546.nuance: செந்நெறி (the red, straight path) is Siva's path. The verse makes grace the condition: those without it keep to முன்னெறி, the paths they began with. சிவனெனப் பெற்றார் (gained the state of being called Siva) anticipates sayujyam.

1547.reading: If one knows how to reach and how to gain the light standing within, there is no quarrel at all; the poor in mind do not know how to end there, in the fire that is the way of cutting off.
1547.nuance: பிணக்கொன்றும் இல்லை (no quarrel at all) answers the chapter's title: the sects' quarrel ends in the inner light, not in argument. வங்கி (fire, vahni) in line 3 is obscure; tradition may read it as the inner fire of yoga.

1548.reading: There is one way to walk the path; the world listens to the fancies of those who walk astray; removing the grief that walks in whirlpools, even those who walk in blame may come to praise.
1548.nuance: நட (walk) runs through every line. கழிநடக்குண்டவர் (those who walk to excess, or along the backwaters) and பரவல் (praise, or spreading) are uncertain; the last line may also mean that the grief spreads to those who walk in blame.

1549.reading: When the great austerity that went the right way abides, cutting away the clinging of strong deeds that bring blame, and leaving the course of the strong deeds that follow, if one goes in due order, one stands before the Lord of the celestials.
1549.nuance: வழி (way) is repeated, and வழிசெல்லும் வல்வினை may be 'the deeds that go with one on the way'. உழி is read as 'in due order' or 'at the right time'. The end is to stand before the Lord, not to become him.

links.note: 725 says the Highest has made the body his temple; 1530 faults the six sects for not seeing the God who stands within the body. The doctrine of 725 becomes the charge against the sects.
1530 says the sects miss the God within the body; 1547 says that once one knows how to reach the light standing within, the quarrel among sects ends of itself.

The Kural calls understanding seeing the true thing in whatever thing, of whatever kind; Tirumular tells people to drop the claim that this or that sect is good and seek the God beyond the forms. Both look past the label to the thing.

source_issues: 1535 line 3, முண்ணின் றழியு முயன்றிலராதலான், may be a misprint for உண்ணின்று.
1534: the word division யறையே சிவமாந் / தவம் is uncertain.
